description: Erection of a part single, part double storey rear extension and conversion of existing 3-bedroom dwelling into 2 x 1-bedroom flats. (part retrospective)
decision_conditions: The conversion of the existing four-bedroom dwelling into 2 x 2 bed self contained units would result in the loss of a residential unit that is suitable and appropriately sized for a family. The proposal would therefore unacceptably undermine the supply of family housing within the Borough for which there is an identified need, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H10 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The conversion of the existing four-bedroom dwelling into 2 x 2 bed self contained units would result in the loss of a residential unit that is suitable and appropriately sized for a family. The proposal would therefore unacceptably undermine the supply of family housing within the Borough for which there is an identified need, contrary to Policies DMH 1 and DMH 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy H10 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

By virtue of the scale, bulk. eaves height and flat roofed design,  the proposed first floor rear extension both individually and when combined with the existing extensions, would result in a dominant, incongruous and visually obtrusive form of development which would cause significant harm to the character, appearance and visual amenities of the pair of semi-detached dwellings and the surrounding area, contrary to Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One- Strategic Policies (2012), Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two- Development Management Policies (2020), Policies D1, D3 and D4 of the London Plan and the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development fails to provide safe and policy compliant access, parking and cycle storage. The proposed parking layout fails to incorporate essential safety features which are fundamental to reducing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian collisions and ensuring safe ingress and egress from the site. In addition, the proposed layout fails to provide unobstructed access to the flats and cycle stores. The proposal fails to meet standards of functionality and accessibility, contrary to Policies T4 and T5 of the London Plan (2021), Policies DMT 2, DMT 5 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020) and the London Borough Of Hillingdon Domestic Vehicle Footway Crossover Policy (DVFC) 4.7.1 Pedestrian Visibility (2022).

The proposal would provide an indoor living area of an unsatisfactory quality for the future occupiers of the proposed first floor flat and would therefore give rise to a substandard form of living accommodation to the detriment of the amenity of future occupiers in conflict with Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 16 of the Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020).

The proposed development fails to provide private outdoor amenity space of sufficient size, quality and usability, contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020). The arrangement of the amenity space, including access and layout, does not meet the policy requirement for well-located, private, and functional outdoor areas for future occupants.
